question: A 30-year-old woman ingested a large quantity of a toilet-bowl cleaner (concentrated HCl) 45 minutes ago. She is conscious with severe oral burns, drooling, and inability to swallow. Which of the following interventions is CONTRAINDICATED?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Adequate analgesia is an important early step in corrosive poisoning management — pain control is appropriate.

Correct — CONTRAINDICATED. Gastric lavage and induced vomiting are absolutely contraindicated in corrosive poisoning. Passing a tube or inducing emesis re-exposes the already-damaged oesophageal and oropharyngeal mucosa to the corrosive, worsening injury and risking perforation.
Endoscopy (within 12–24 hours) is the key investigation to grade oesophageal injury (Zargar classification) and guide prognosis. It is recommended, not contraindicated.
IV fluid resuscitation and keeping the patient nil by mouth are standard and appropriate management steps in corrosive poisoning.

overallFeedback.feedback: In corrosive poisoning, the key contraindications are gastric lavage and induced vomiting. Never neutralise the corrosive either — exothermic reactions cause thermal injury.
Well done. The single most dangerous management error in corrosive poisoning is inducing vomiting or passing a nasogastric tube — both re-expose damaged mucosa and risk perforation.
